questions.q:
Five cards are drawn successively with replacement from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards; find the probability that all the five cards are spades.



Five cards are drawn successively with replacement from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards; find the probability that none is a spade.
questions.solution:
Let X denote number of spade cards.

p = probability of drawing a spade card from a pack of 52 cards.

Since there are 13 spade cards in the pack of 52 cards,

∴ p = `13/52 = 1/4`  and q = 1 − p = `1 - 1/4 = 3/4`

Given, n = 5

∴ `X ~ B(5, 1/4)`

The p.m.f. of X is given by

P(X = x) = `"^nC_x  p^x  q^(n - x)`

i.e. p(x) = `"^5C_x  (1/4)^x  (3/5)^(5 - x)`, x = 0, 1, 2, ..., 5

P(all five cards are spades):

= P(X = 5) = p(5) = `"^5C_5(1/4)^5(3/4)^(5 - 5)`

`= 1(1/4)^5(3/4)^0`

`= 1 xx 1/1024 xx 1`

= `1/1024`

= `1/4^5`

Hence, the probability of all the five cards are spades is `1/4^5`.

questions.q: If the mean and variance of a binomial distribution are 18 and 12 respectively, then n = ______.
questions.solution:
If the mean and variance of a binomial distribution are 18 and 12 respectively, then n = 54.

Explanation:

Mean = np = 18  ...(i)

Variance = npq = 12  ...(ii)

∴ `(npq)/(np) = 12/18`

∴ q = `2/3`

∴ p = 1 − q

= `1 - 2/3`

= `1/3`

np = 18  ...[From eqn. (i)]

∴ `n(1/3) = 18`

∴ n = 18 × 3

∴ n = 54

questions.q: Let the probability mass function (p.m.f.) of a random variable X be P(X = x) = `""^4C_x (5/9)^x xx (4/9)^(4 - x)`, for x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 then E(X) is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Let the probability mass function (p.m.f.) of a random variable X be P(X = x) = `""^4C_x (5/9)^x xx (4/9)^(4 - x)`, for x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 then E(X) is equal to `underlinebb(20/9)`.

Explanation:

P (X = x) is binomial distribution with n = 4, p = `5/9` and q = `4/9`

E(X) = np

= `4 xx (5/9)`

= `20/9`

questions.q: A die is thrown 6 times. If ‘getting an odd number’ is a success, find the probability of 5 successes.
questions.solution:
Let X = number of successes, i.e., number of odd numbers.

p = probability of getting an odd number in a single throw of a die

∴ p = `3/6 = 1/2` and

q = `1 - "p" = 1 - 1/2 = 1/2`

Given: n = 6

∴ X ∼ B`(6, 1/2)`

The p.m.f. of X is given by

`p("X = x") = "^nC_x  p^x  q^(n - x)`

i.e. p(x) = `"^6C_x (1/2)^x (1/2)^(6 - x)`

` = "^6C_x (1/2)^6,` x = 0, 1, 2, ...,6

P(5 successes) = P[X = 5]

`= p(5) = "^6C_5 (1/2)^6`

`= "^6C_1 xx 1/64`        ...`[because ""^nC_x = "^nC_(n - x)]`

`= 6/64`

= `3/32`

Hence, the probability of 5 successes is `3/32`

questions.q: A die is thrown 6 times. If ‘getting an odd number’ is a success, find the probability of at least 5 successes.
questions.solution:
Let X = number of successes, i.e. number of odd numbers.

p = probability of getting an odd number in a single throw of a die

∴ p = `3/6 = 1/2` and q = `1 - "p" = 1 - 1/2 = 1/2`

Given: n = 6

∴ X ∼ B`(6, 1/2)`

The p.m.f. of X is given by

`p("X = x") = "^nC_x  p^x  q^(n - x)`

i.e. p(x) = `"^6C_x (1/2)^x (1/2)^(6 - x)`

` = "^6C_x (1/2)^6,` x = 0, 1, 2, ...,6

P(at least 5 successes) = P[X ≥ 5]

= p(5) + p(6)

`= ""^6C_5 (1/2)^6 + "^6C_6 (1/2)^6`

`= (""^6C_5 + "^6C_6) (1/2)^6`

`= (6 + 1) 1/64 = 7/64`

Hence, the probability of at least 5 successes is `7/64`.
